lead: New offering terms supersede earlier estimates, while model evaluations distinguish projections from measured task cost. Coding gates and a disputed false alert keep attention on what verification actually covers.

sections.title: Offering terms replace earlier estimates
sections.intro: A primary pricing announcement gives a newer share count, while regional-tranche and investment-strategy reports remain separately sourced.

sections.title: Speed projections meet measured task costs
sections.intro: Neon preference projections, evaluator measurements and launch-price reporting answer different questions.

sections.title: Verification is bounded by the checks
sections.intro: Coding gates, streaming exports and investigation workflows describe useful designs without proving every result correct.

sections.title: A false alert and institutional choices
sections.intro: Plaintiff allegations, school procurement discussions and government cybercrime spending require distinct evidence.

sections.title: Reconstruction, creative credit and value capture
sections.intro: An inversion abstract, production notes and a historical analogy leave important questions open.

sections.title: Word boundaries and compact illustrations
sections.intro: Two small tools make concrete representation choices, with vendor benchmarks and explicit scope limits.

sections.title: Corrections and promotions complicate model comparisons
sections.intro: A roundup correction and temporary prices show why a launch ranking is not a stable universal ordering.

sections.title: Investigations and uncertain identities
sections.intro: A contested identity link, reported agent concerns and an opened investigation must not become findings of guilt or confirmed leaks.

sections.title: Institutional choices under pressure
sections.intro: Campus objections, sovereign-model debates and travel hurdles have different sources and unresolved practical outcomes.

sections.title: Funding and employee perspectives remain separate
sections.intro: Laboratory financing, IPO allocations and interview impressions measure neither scientific success nor consensus.

sections.title: What people can turn off or keep local
sections.intro: Canva controls, a non-generative writing pitch and local-model advocacy approach user choice from different directions.

sections.title: Running a product is more than generating code
sections.intro: Model-training platforms, incident models and continuous maintenance tools need separate checks for model quality and system behavior.

sections.title: Cache economics and voice transport
sections.intro: Session switching and speech delivery have workload-specific costs that simple per-token or latency slogans miss.

sections.title: Historical spending is not future capacity
sections.intro: Annualized compute estimates, proposed orbital servers and grid projections measure different stages of infrastructure.

sections.title: Arguments about power and the future
sections.intro: Engineering objections, timeline forecasts, policy visions and labor and copyright debates remain distinct kinds of evidence.

sections.title: Commerce, craft and scarce shares
sections.intro: Unreadable interviews and financial excerpts support only limited conclusions about how value and access are distributed.

sections.title: Cyberattack attribution needs an accessible record
sections.intro: A short indexed report does not establish the causal contribution of an intrusion tool.

sections.title: A first trade is not a closing valuation
sections.intro: The offering price, opening trade and closing price describe different stages, while share-count conventions change the valuation.

sections.title: What counts as checking a result
sections.intro: A physics announcement, missing table generators and verification arguments each need checks suited to their claims.

sections.title: Agent controls and the worlds used to test them
sections.intro: Computer-use previews and simulated websites address different layers of operational risk.

sections.title: Working conditions and public opposition
sections.intro: Platform labor, career anxiety and protests describe distinct kinds of evidence about AI’s social effects.

sections.title: Products still need their own evidence
sections.intro: A design canvas, molecule models, a game review and a proposed device price cannot substitute for tests of their different promises.

sections.title: Local speech has modularity tradeoffs
sections.intro: An edited interview describes local control and component reuse without establishing universal benchmark parity.
